claimBoundary.coreClaim: A fresh acknowledged message mutation remains journal-backed through the active-generation window, while reads use the authoritative dirty cache and cache-index population remains available during later compaction.

Cold storage reads during deferred compaction

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: Checkpoint-tracked message collections ignored the journal age policy and began a large primary rewrite 750 ms after each message, causing reply and memory-capture writes to queue behind Pi disk work.
contractLaneGate.producer: src-tauri/crates/storage deferred flush scheduler and journal compaction policy
contractLaneGate.consumer: Conversation and Roleplay generation completion plus unrelated cold cache reads
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: An acknowledged journal is the durable boundary during an active turn; primary-file compaction is background maintenance and must wait for idle or a bounded threshold.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: Deferred flush honors the same age, entry, and byte policy for tracked collections, defaults the idle age to 60 seconds, and takes an Arc cached-row snapshot before releasing the cache lock.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The storage crate owns journal durability, compaction scheduling, cache authority, and cache locking.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not hide the pause in UI pending state, skip durable writes, or weaken startup recovery.
regressionProof: The active-generation test failed before implementation because a fresh tracked message journal immediately rewrote messages.json.
The cold-cache test failed before implementation because the compaction snapshot held the cache lock.
Both focused tests and all 141 storage tests pass after the storage-owner changes.
